title: Even quotient component is a chain map
statement: For a commutative ring A, a bicomplex K of A-modules with zero positive columns, short complexes S_a and isomorphisms e_a from their middle complexes to column -a, define the explicit component map by restricting the lower-column map to F_(2j+1) and then composing with the cokernel projection of F_(2j) → F_(2j+1). For each natural j and each cochain relation k+1=l, these components commute with the differentials from the shift by j of (S_j).X₁ to that cokernel.

General cokernel maps and universal properties, not this explicit filtration quotient.
No msearch hits. Local search of homology modules found filtration quotient users and the odd quotient, but no prior even component identification.

lean.statement:
theorem evenQuotientComponent_comm (j : ℕ) (k l : ℤ)
    (hkl : (ComplexShape.up ℤ).Rel k l) :
    evenQuotientComponent K S e h_positive j k ≫
      (cokernel (step K S e h_positive (2 * j))).d k l =
    ((CategoryTheory.shiftFunctor (CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ) (j : ℤ)).obj
      (S j).X₁).d k l ≫ evenQuotientComponent K S e h_positive j l

proof.text: Restrict the lower-column maps to the odd filtration term using range membership. The horizontal differential lands in an earlier full column of the even term, or is zero for j=0 because the positive column is zero. The vertical differential is the endpoint differential followed by the lower-column map, with sign (-1)^j. Inclusions of submodules are injective, so the restricted differential equality follows. Compose with the cokernel projection; its chain-map equation and cokernel condition kill the horizontal term and give commutation with the shifted differential. All these steps are proved in Lean.
